title: NFPA 70 (NEC) 2023, Chapter 9 Table 1 with its Notes, and Informative Annex C Tables C.1 to C.13(A): the most conductors of one size in each trade size of conduit and tubing

source.attribution: Source: NFPA 70 (NEC) 2023, Chapter 9 Table 1 and Informative Annex C, Tables C.1 to C.13(A), as NFPA's 2026-cycle records print them — retrieved Nov 2026

notes.annex_c: Note 1: Informative Annex C gives the maximum number of conductors and fixture wires, all of the same size (total cross-sectional area including insulation), in each trade size.
notes.complete_systems: Note 2: Table 1 applies only to complete conduit or tubing systems, not to sections that protect exposed wiring and cable from physical damage.
notes.egc_counted: Note 3: equipment grounding or bonding conductors, where installed, are included in the fill, at their actual dimensions (insulated or bare).

nipple.text: Note 4: a nipple between boxes, cabinets and similar enclosures, not longer than 600 mm (24 in.) and not counting connectors, may be filled to 60 percent of its cross-sectional area, and the 310.15(C)(1) adjustment factors need not apply to it.

notes.mixed_sizes: Note 6: for conductors of different sizes, use actual dimensions or Tables 5 and 5A for the conductors and Table 4 for the conduit or tubing.

round_up.text: Note 7: for conductors all of one size, a calculated count whose decimal is 0.8 or more is rounded up to the next whole number; for a single conductor, one is permitted when the calculation gives 0.8 or more.

notes.cables: Note 9: a multiconductor cable, optical fiber cable or flexible cord of two or more conductors counts as a single conductor; an elliptical cable is figured as a circle of its major diameter; single conductors without an overall covering are not a cable.

jamming.text: Informational Note No. 2: when pulling three conductors or cables into a raceway, jamming can occur if the ratio of the raceway's inside diameter to the conductor's or cable's outside diameter is between 2.8 and 3.2; with four or more the probability is very low.

notes.stranding: Note 10: Table 5 values are worst-case round concentric-lay stranding (solid grouped with it); compact stranding is in Table 5A; known actual dimensions may be used.

table_1.revision_2026: FR-7763 (2026 First Draft) changes the wording of Informational Note No. 1 and Notes 7 and 8 only; Table 1's percentages are unmarked.

notes: Counts are the 2023 Annex C values exactly as printed; null is the table's dash (no such trade size, or no such compact conductor).

Table C.9 (RMC): the record prints no dash in the 3/8 column on two rows (THHN, THWN, THWN-2 500 kcmil; FEP, FEPB, PFA, PFAH, TFE 2 AWG); RMC has no 3/8 trade size in the table, and the twelve printed values line up under 1/2 to 6, so the 3/8 cell is the dash.
Table C.7 (LFNC-C): the record labels the THHN rows 'THHW, THWN, THWN-2'; they are in the THHN position of every other table and are kept as THHN, THWN, THWN-2.
Fixture wires (the FIXTURE WIRES part of each table) are not carried.
The tables are informative: they apply Table 1 (40 percent for over two conductors), Table 4 and Table 5 (Table 5A for the (A) tables) with Note 7's 0.8 rounding.
Table 4 (other than IMC) and Table 5 are not verified here (nec-ch9-table4.json holds IMC only): conductors of different sizes are not calculated.
